conventions.commits: Conventional Commits with type(scope): subject; GPG-signed with --signoff; types: feat, fix, docs, refactor, test, chore
conventions.testing: Unit tests in module files (cfg[test]); integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/; each language module has test_*_element_query_happy_path, test_*_extract_inheritance, test_defuse_query_write_site
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy -- -D warnings, cargo deny check advisories licenses; workspace lints enforce undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test exemptions via cfg_attr)
conventions.error_handling: No unwrap/expect in production paths; use Option/Result with .and_then, .map, pattern matching; SAFETY comments required for unsafe blocks

patterns: Each language module defines ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, and optional REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY as &str constants
ELEMENT_QUERY captures @function and @class nodes with @*_name captures for identifiers
DEFUSE_QUERY uses @write.* and @read.* capture prefixes to mark definition/use sites
extract_inheritance walks parent nodes to find extends/implements clauses and returns Vec<String>
Language registration in mod.rs get_language_info() match arm includes all query strings and handler functions
EXTENSION_MAP in lang.rs maps file extensions to language identifiers; supported_languages() lists all available languages
Minimal languages (CSS, HTML, YAML) omit DEFUSE_QUERY and handler functions; full languages (Java, Python, Kotlin) include them

related_issues.title: Add PHP language support via tree-sitter-php
related_issues.relevance: Direct task: implement PHP language handler following Java pattern

constraints: All languages unconditionally compiled in; no feature gates for individual languages
tree-sitter-php uses LANGUAGE_PHP constant (not LANGUAGE) unlike other tree-sitter-* crates
PHP grammar uses base_clause and class_interface_clause as child nodes, not fields on class_declaration
DEFUSE_QUERY is required for semantic analysis (def-use site extraction); must be provided for PHP
New language modules must include SPDX header: // SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 aptu-coder contributors and // SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
test_coverage: Existing language modules have unit tests for: element_query_happy_path (verifies ELEMENT_QUERY matches expected declarations), extract_inheritance (verifies extends/implements extraction), defuse_query_write_site (verifies DEFUSE_QUERY captures write sites). Integration tests in crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/integration_tests.rs verify language_for_extension() and get_language_info() for all registered languages.

library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE_PHP constant; Grammar defines class_declaration (fields: name, body, attributes; children: base_clause, class_interface_clause), interface_declaration, trait_declaration, function_definition, method_declaration, enum_declaration
library_findings.notes: PHP grammar does not use field names for inheritance; instead base_clause and class_interface_clause are child nodes. base_clause contains 'extends' keyword + names; class_interface_clause contains 'implements' keyword + names. Enums can implement interfaces via class_interface_clause.

library_findings.relevant_api: Query API for tree-sitter queries; Node API for traversing tree; child_by_field_name(), child(), parent(), kind(), start_byte(), end_byte()
library_findings.notes: Queries use @capture syntax; field names must match grammar definition exactly. PHP grammar differs from Java in that inheritance is via child nodes, not fields.

approaches.name: Minimal PHP Handler (CSS-style)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY and CALL_QUERY; no DEFUSE_QUERY, no inheritance extraction. Register in mod.rs and lang.rs. Add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml.
pros: Simplest implementation; fewest lines of code
Matches CSS/HTML/YAML pattern for languages with limited semantic analysis
cons: No def-use site analysis (DEFUSE_QUERY required by issue #1864)
No inheritance tracking; breaks semantic analysis for OOP code
Incomplete compared to Java/Python/Kotlin reference implementations

approaches.name: Full PHP Handler with DEFUSE_QUERY (Recommended)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY, and extract_inheritance(). Handle PHP's base_clause/class_interface_clause child nodes. Register in mod.rs and lang.rs. Add tree-sitter-php to Cargo.toml.
pros: Enables full semantic analysis (def-use sites, inheritance tracking)
Supports all PHP declaration kinds: classes, interfaces, traits, functions, methods, enums
cons: More code than minimal approach (~250-350 lines)
Requires careful handling of PHP's grammar differences (base_clause/class_interface_clause)
More complex inheritance extraction due to non-field-based extends/implements

approaches.name: Full Handler with Extended Features
approaches.description: Full PHP handler plus find_method_for_receiver, find_receiver_type, extract_function_name handlers for advanced method resolution. Support property promotion and named arguments.
pros: Maximum semantic capability for PHP code analysis
Enables method call resolution across inheritance hierarchies
cons: Requires deep understanding of PHP grammar edge cases
May be over-engineered if issue only requires DEFUSE_QUERY

recommendation: Approach 2 (Full PHP Handler with DEFUSE_QUERY). The issue explicitly requires DEFUSE_QUERY support, and the Java reference implementation demonstrates this is the standard pattern. PHP's grammar differences (base_clause/class_interface_clause as child nodes) are manageable and well-documented. This approach balances completeness with reasonable implementation complexity, and aligns with the project's existing language integration standards.
language_info_struct_citation:
pub struct LanguageInfo {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub language: Language,
    pub element_query: &'static str,
    pub call_query: &'static str,
    pub reference_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub import_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub impl_trait_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defuse_query: Option<&'static str>,
    pub extract_function_name: Option<ExtractFunctionNameHandler>,
    pub find_method_for_receiver: Option<FindMethodForReceiverHandler>,
    pub find_receiver_type: Option<FindReceiverTypeHandler>,
    pub extract_inheritance: Option<ExtractInheritanceHandler>,
}
element_query_draft:
(
function_definition
  name: (name) @function_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
inheritance_walk_citation: For a class_declaration node in tree-sitter-php: (1) Call node.child() in loop to iterate all children; (2) Find child with kind() == 'base_clause' (represents 'extends'); (3) Within base_clause, iterate children to find name nodes and extract their text via source[start_byte()..end_byte()]; (4) Find child with kind() == 'class_interface_clause' (represents 'implements'); (5) Within class_interface_clause, iterate children to find name nodes and extract text. This pattern is derived from tree-sitter-php grammar source at https://github.com/tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php/blob/master/common/define-grammar.js where base_clause and class_interface_clause are defined as seq() rules containing names, not as field names on class_declaration.
